clue.text: Secure clever addition to funny trick: going back in time?

indicators.note: the following pieces are tacked on after the trick

parts.note: an antic is a playful or absurd caper
to lock something is to secure it
wise means clever or sagacious

explanation.surface: Someone tops off a comic stunt with a clever twist that seems to turn back the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: moving against the clock hands looks like going backwards through time.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock hands sweep forward, so turning them the opposite way is jokingly described as travelling back in time.

clue.text: Old taffeta nicely repaired, with love

indicators.note: repaired implies something being put back together differently, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An old taffeta garment, neatly mended, given with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something affectionately means doing it with love and tenderness.

clue.text: Drink to cut no end

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: Someone drinks to cutting things off endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a drink, often mixed with gin.

clue.text: First of classic spectacles in which king is introduced to the people

definitions.text: First of classic spectacles in which king is introduced to the people

indicators.note: only the opening letter of classic is taken
the king's letter is put into the middle of the spectacles

parts.note: two Os look like a pair of spectacles
R is short for rex, king
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A grand ceremony where a new monarch is presented to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a coronation is a classic spectacle presenting a king to his people.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation is the ceremonial crowning of a monarch before the people.

clue.text: Love little accepted by communist that's made revolution

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the communist takes in the small piece, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: Red is a common term for a communist
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Romance, in small doses, is welcomed by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests communist politics, but here it is a circuit in space.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle around a body, completing a revolution.

clue.text: Having relations with royalty not good

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: kingship is the state of royalty

explanation.surface: Royalty mixing with others is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is the state of being related, of having family relations.

clue.text: Snag commonly an irritation

indicators.note: common speech drops its aitches, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a hitch is a snag

explanation.surface: A snag is a common annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritation of the skin, or figuratively a nagging annoyance.

clue.text: Living for pleasure, tipping part of neck back and injecting one fix

indicators.note: the remedy is put into the reversed neck part
tipping something back turns it over, so the word runs backwards
completes the instruction to read the neck part backwards

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck
I is the roman numeral one
a cure is a fix for an ailment

explanation.surface: A hedonist throws their head back and takes a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean devotes themselves to sensual pleasure, especially good food and drink.

clue.text: Through to the next round, with hardly a ringing endorsement?

definitions.text: Through to the next round, with hardly a ringing endorsement?

parts.words: Through to the next round, with hardly a ringing endorsement?
parts.note: a boxer rescued at the end of a round by the gong, escaping rather than winning convincingly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means rescued at the last moment, originally a boxer spared by the gong.

clue.text: Better-quality magistrate?

definitions.meaning: comparative of fine, meaning of higher quality
jokingly, one who imposes fines on offenders

explanation.definitionFit: Finer is the comparative of fine; a magistrate fines people, so is whimsically one who fines.

clue.text: Bishop leads united church in a delicate service

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
made one means united
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop heads a merged congregation at a refined act of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks ecclesiastical next to bishop and church, but here it is a tea or dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner or tea service made of fine translucent porcelain is a delicate set of tableware.

clue.text: Clown gets head nervous, where prizes are given away

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
nut is slang for the head
shy means timid or nervous

explanation.surface: A clown loses their nerve at a fairground prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: A COCONUT SHY is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts to win them.
explanation.definitionFit: At this fairground stall, knocking a coconut off its stand wins it as a prize.

clue.text: Old invader gets stick out with energy

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ancient raider pokes something out forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jutes were a Germanic people who invaded Britain in the fifth century.

clue.text: Pub painter did almost nothing for one covering the region

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pub artist who barely did anything for a regional client.
explanation.definitionFit: Local radio is a broadcaster serving a particular area, covering the news of its region.

clue.text: Pushed home, speaking of having vision

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: signals that the next word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sighted means able to see

explanation.surface: Someone talks about having vision while being driven home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushed home' looks like the definition, but home gives IN; 'speaking of' turns SIGHTED into a sound-alike spelt CITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or push them into action, so incited means pushed.

clue.text: Out of public view, blunt-spoken and hurt to lose power

parts.note: curt means brusque, blunt

indicators.note: losing the power letter means it is taken out

parts.note: pained means hurt
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from the public eye after brusque remarks and a loss of influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curtained is screened off by curtains, hidden from public view.

clue.text: Saw demonstrator bashed in the head

parts.note: one who proves or demonstrates something is a prover

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of bashed is used

explanation.surface: Someone saw a protester being hit on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as a verb in the past tense, but it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a pithy traditional adage.

clue.text: In space, restricts new weapons

parts.note: arrows are weapons shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Fresh armaments limit room in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow something is to make it less wide, restricting it physically in its extent.

clue.text: Policemen eat quiet meals

indicators.note: the policemen take the quiet letter inside them

parts.note: supers is short for superintendents, senior policemen
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Officers eat their dinners in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppers are evening meals.

clue.text: Stand abrupt question? I don't think so

parts.note: a curt 'What?' is an abrupt question
a dismissive 'not' means I don't think so

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand against a blunt question by refusing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A WHATNOT is a stand of open shelves for ornaments; 'Stand' looks like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a piece of furniture: a stand with open shelves for displaying small objects.

clue.text: Daughter toils to ply needle up in fashionable area

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the pieces backwards

parts.note: toils are nets or snares, a toil being a net
to sew is to ply a needle

explanation.surface: A daughter labours over her needlework in a smart district.
explanation.walkthrough: The WEST END is London's fashionable shopping and theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is its smart district of shops, theatres and fashion.

clue.text: Feature of weather that's finally as changed

annotationWithheld.why: Feature of weather that's finally as changed (4) gives THAW, but no parse found: the W has no clear source, and 'that's finally as changed' does not yield the letters without one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Feature of weather that's finally as changed

clue.text: What greengrocer's offering here with unusual accuracy?

definitions.text: What greengrocer's offering here with unusual accuracy?

parts.words: What greengrocer's offering here with unusual accuracy?
parts.note: greengrocers are mocked for stray punctuation on signs like 'apple's'; in the word greengrocer's itself the mark is for once correct

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark in greengrocer's, so often misused by grocers, is properly placed in this possessive.

clue.text: Indian perhaps one is to tap up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one
S stands for is, as in the contraction 's
a rap is a tap or knock

explanation.surface: An Indian person, perhaps, is someone to knock up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a member of a Zoroastrian community in India, so an Indian by example.

clue.text: Staff feeding line to poet

indicators.note: the line letter is fed into the poet's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet

explanation.surface: Employees supply a line of verse to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is a long staff or rod.

clue.text: Wheel teacher in with no assistant to you

indicators.note: the teacher is placed inside the word for solitary

parts.note: lone means alone, with no helper
a don is a university teacher
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A teacher on their own turns to you at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The LONDON EYE is the giant observation wheel on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This landmark is a huge Ferris-style observation wheel on London's South Bank.

clue.text: Lamentation as energy transmission system is in fallback

indicators.note: falling back means running backwards, so the joined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the national grid is the system transmitting electricity

explanation.surface: A mournful note as the power network falls back on emergency supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead.

clue.text: Likes toddlers turned out in best gear

indicators.note: turned out suggests reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Small children who enjoy being smartly turned out in their finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like the definition (dressed up), but it signals the anagram of LIKES TODDLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed to kill is an idiom for wearing one's smartest, most striking clothes.
